newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar ends on lows but seen supported.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar ends on lows but seen supported.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar was ending on its lows on Wednesday but dealers said it was well supported around US$0.7085 and they expected buying on any dips.
The currency closed at 0.7083/90 and 67.57 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.7106/13 and 67.80 at the opening.

"It feels like a long local market. We've seen plenty of selling from Hong Kong over the last two days, that's beginning to weigh on the market. I just think the market's got a little bit ahead of itself," a Wellington dealer said.
He said a large local corporate had also emerged as a seller.
An Auckland dealer said comments by New Zealand First leader Winston Peters that the recent rise of the Kiwi gave urgency to coalition-building talks was seen as negative for the currency.
"Domestic guys are looking at that and seeing that as really quite bearish for the currency. He (Peters) still politically holds the key card and from my point of view that is the focus."

Peters said repeatedly during the recent election campaign he wanted to drive the New Zealand dollar down to help exporters. Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen also called on Tuesday for a monetary policy easing.
The dealer said taken together, their statements indicated the Kiwi and interest rates would come off.

Nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power after the inconclusive election, held coalition talks on Wednesday with both Labour and the caretaker National Party government. Peters also commented he believed the talks could be wrapped up within six weeks.
The Kiwi traded a US$0.7085-7110 range on the day.
